title: Orion Edge - Latency & Burst Throughput Discovery
summary: Initial discovery to understand Orion Edge's p95 latency targets for streaming agent responses, burst concurrency needs for peak inference (token/sec targets), and constraints around private deployment (VPC + KMS). Redwood AE+SE walked through architecture options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and proposed a short benchmarking pilot and a canary plan for Dedicated pools.
next_steps: Redwood to propose pilot benchmark plan with target test matrix by 2026-04-01
Orion to share sample prompts + expected qps profile
Schedule Dedicated capacity sizing call w/infra (Priya + Jon) week of 2026-04-06
action_items: Marcus Lee - send pilot test matrix and pricing assumptions (due 2026-04-01)
Mina Park - share 2 weeks of request traces + sample prompts (due 2026-03-30)
Priya Nair - prepare Dedicated sizing worksheet and initial config suggestions (due 2026-04-05)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood Solutions), Alex Torres (CTO, Orion Edge), Mina Park (ML Eng), Jon Reyes (Infra Lead), Sasha Liu (Product)

SUMMARY: quick discovery re: p95 goals for streaming: Orion wants sub-350ms p95 on short-turn agent replies, and p95 under 800ms for longer multi-turn streaming. Also they have unpredictable burst windows (event-driven: up to 250 concurrent streams for ~30s every 10 minutes).

[00:00] Marcus Lee: hey everyone, thanks for carving time. i'm Marcus from Redwood, i'm the account lead. with me is priya our systems eng. jordan from solutions will chime on ops. quick round robin?
[00:12] Alex Torres: alex here, cto at orion edge. we run an inference layer for edge agents, product is latency sensitive.
[00:17] Mina Park: hey this is mina, ML eng. i'll share traces after.
[00:20] Jon Reyes: jon infra. we care about VPC, encryption, and predictable bursts.
[00:26] Priya Nair: great, quick agenda: p95 targets, concurrency/burst, streaming vs non-streaming, private vs hosted constraints, next steps. sound good?
[00:33] Sasha Liu: perfect.

---

[02:05] Marcus Lee: can you give us numbers — what are your current p95 today and the desired?
[02:12] Alex Torres: today we self-host on a mix of A100s and T4s for different models, p95 for short responses is around 420-480ms if we hit the GPU local cache, but it spikes to 1.2s when cold or during compaction. target we want is 300-350ms p95 for single-turn assistant style responses sub ~120 tokens. longer summaries can be up to 800ms p95.
[02:45] Priya Nair: okay, so short-turn p95 300-350ms, longer 800ms p95. what's the concurrency shape?
[02:53] Mina Park: baseline steady qps of 30 requests/s, but bursts: during event windows we get bursts that translate to ~200-250 concurrent active streams for about 20-40 seconds. Those are streaming responses — token streaming at 15-30 tokens/sec per stream.
[03:14] Marcus Lee: streaming at 15-30 tok/sec, 250 concurrent, so aggregate tokens/sec could peak — quick math — 3,750 to 7,500 tokens/sec.
[03:25] Jon Reyes: yep, and we can't buffer those bursts — user perceived latencies must stay tight. also requirement: everything must be able to run in our VPC for certain customers; KMS-managed keys, SOC2 audit logs, SSO via Okta.

[05:06] Priya Nair: that helps. two things to call out: 1) streaming has different perf characteristics because of the KV cache and continuous batching, and 2) p95 is usually driven by queuing in batching windows or lock-step scheduling when we hit max batch size. we need to know average sequence length and typical past prefix caching hit rate.
[05:33] Mina Park: avg sequence length for these interactions is 90 tokens; short-replies are 40 tokens. prefix cache hit probably 20-30% today.

[06:10] Marcus Lee: for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — quick pros/cons: Hosted for easiest onboarding but shared capacity and rate limits, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and burst buffers, Private (VPC/On-prem) gives you full control and KMS but needs more ops. For your p95 goals likely Dedicated or Private.
[06:40] Alex Torres: cost sensitivity is real though; we are a mid-stage startup. how much more is Dedicated vs Hosted roughly for our shape?
[06:50] Marcus Lee: depends on sizing. for your peak tokens/sec we'd recommend a small Dedicated pool with burst capacity. ballpark: the incremental committed monthly can be 2-4x hosted for the guaranteed headroom, but unit cost per token often drops with Dedicated. we'll send numbers.

[08:12] Priya Nair: technical question for jon — what's your egress network topology in the VPC and do you have strict egress controls that would block streaming websocket endpoints?
[08:22] Jon Reyes: we have an egress proxy and strict security groups. We can open dedicated endpoints per subnet for Redwood Private but for Hosted we'd need to route through our proxy — not ideal.
[08:35] Priya Nair: noted. Private deployment would avoid that extra hop.

[09:00] Sasha Liu: one more: what are typical failure modes you see in production?
[09:05] Mina Park: often we see token generation stalls when KV cache misses and the model has to fetch long KV context; also garbage collector related pauses on our management layer, and spikes when multiple clients request long completions simultaneously.

[10:20] Priya Nair: for the KV cache misses, Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV caching and can keep working set hot for those frequently requested prompts. We also have config knobs for max batch size and per-model execution lanes to isolate long-running requests.
[10:40] Marcus Lee: question for alex — for success criteria beyond raw p95 latency, do you have SLOs around error rates?
[10:48] Alex Torres: yes, SLO: <1% 5xx, and 99.95% availability during business hours, and auditability for user data access.

[12:03] Jon Reyes: regarding the bursts — is there an auto-fallback if Dedicated pool saturates? we don't want dropped requests.
[12:12] Priya Nair: yes, Redwood supports smart routing + automatic fallback to lighter/quantized variants or Hosted spillover depending on policy. for strict private-only customers we can configure queueing or pre-provisioned burst capacity. fallback paths can be by model or by region.

[13:40] Marcus Lee: let's get into benchmarking — we propose a two-week pilot where the Redwood team runs token/sec and streaming latency benchmarks against a mirrored workload:
- test matrix: short-turn 40 token responses at 300qps steady state; burst profile: 250 concurrent streaming connections for 30s every 10min; long-turn 90-150 token responses at 50qps.
- metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, concurrency, GPU utilization, queue depth, cold vs warm cache runs.

[14:20] Mina Park: sounds good. can you simulate our prefix-caching behavior? we have a heavy-tail distribution of prompts.
[14:27] Priya Nair: yes, we'll parameterize cache hit rates (0%, 25%, 50%) in the pilot. we'll also test quantized model variants for cost-optimized fallbacks.

[15:50] Alex Torres: for streaming token/sec — what's realistic on a single A100 for say a 7B style model?
[15:58] Priya Nair: rough numbers: with optimized kernels and batching, sustained token/sec for a 7B can be in the thousands on a single A100 for generation-only workloads, but streaming with low latency constraints often reduces batching efficiency. so i'd expect 500-2,000 tok/s depending on sequence length and policy. with splitting across multiple GPUs and RDMA/aggregation we can hit higher aggregate ts.
[16:34] Jon Reyes: ok so we'll need to size for worst-case aggregate 7.5k tok/s.

[17:10] Marcus Lee: we should also talk about canaries — a rollout plan if you go Dedicated: start with 10% traffic to Dedicated with auto-fallback to Hosted, monitor p95 and error rate for 48h, then ramp.
[17:26] Alex Torres: agreed. how invasive is Private? ops wise.
[17:34] Jordan Kim: Private deployment requires VPN/VPC peering, a private control plane, and optionally an on-prem package. we have an installation guide; ops overhead is comparable to running a managed service but you own networking and keys. we help with initial setup.

[19:00] Mina Park: about monitoring — do you expose token-level breakdowns? we need to attribute cost per feature.
[19:08] Marcus Lee: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route latency, trace hooks, and you can plug in logs to your SIEM. We'll provide an eval retention for the pilot.

[20:00] Alex Torres: question: what's your quantization story? we want to keep quality high for summaries.
[20:07] Priya Nair: we support 8-bit and 4-bit quantization profiles; Optimize can recommend profiles per workload. for summaries we usually keep higher precision; fallback variants can be quantized for lower-cost retrieval or heuristic responses.

[21:30] Sasha Liu: regulatory: SOC2 and KMS integrations — is audit logging sufficient for our compliance customers?
[21:38] Marcus Lee: yes, we provide audit logs, configurable retention, and KMS/HSM integrations. Private deployments can be configured to use your KMS keys. We'll share our SOC2 report and security whitepaper.

[23:02] Priya Nair: quick technical deep-dive: when streaming, the runtime maintains a KV cache per model shard; we continuously append tokens to the stream as generation proceeds, and to keep p95 low we tune scheduling to prioritize low-latency lanes and small-batch immediate flushes. That trades off throughput but fits your latency SLO.

[25:10] Mina Park: do you have sample configs we can try? we want to test max_batch_size 8 vs 32 and see p95 impact.
[25:20] Priya Nair: yes we'll include a config matrix. For example small-batch config: max_batch 8, lane for streaming, lower batch timeout; throughput config: max_batch 32 with longer batch timeout. We'll measure p95 and tokens/sec for both.

[27:00] Jon Reyes: network jitter will affect token arrival. can Redwood agents compensate for jitter at application layer?
[27:08] Jordan Kim: we provide client-side guidance and SDKs that handle reconnects, backpressure signals, and incremental snapshots so you don't need to re-run long contexts.

[29:30] Marcus Lee: let's cover acceptance criteria for the pilot:
- short-turn p95 <= 350ms (warm cache)
- streaming end-to-end perceived p95 <= 800ms for long-turns
- <1% 5xx and availability >= 99.95%
- benchmarks should include cold-cache and warm-cache runs

[30:10] Alex Torres: that's reasonable; if you can meet that in Dedicated we'll consider a 6mo commit but need numbers.

[31:00] Priya Nair: i'll correlate required GPU headroom to those p95 targets and propose a minimal Dedicated pool. For cost we can show per-token breakouts and how quantized fallbacks reduce spend.

[33:40] Mina Park: one more: do you support model pinning and rollbacks in Dedicated? we need quick rollbacks for regressions.
[33:48] Marcus Lee: yes, rollouts, canary, A/B, automatic fallback on regressions are all supported via the console. We also tie quality monitoring to evals so you can detect regressions quickly.

[35:10] Jon Reyes: about SSO — we use Okta. is SAML available for the Console?
[35:15] Jordan Kim: yes, SAML/Okta integration is supported and we can set up RBAC per-team.

[36:02] Alex Torres: any known gotchas with quantization and streaming?
[36:10] Priya Nair: main gotcha is sometimes quantization increases token-by-token variance causing occasional higher-latency spikes; we recommend keeping high-quality variants for critical paths, use quantized for fallbacks. we'll measure ROUGE/quality in the pilot.

[38:00] Marcus Lee: timeline — propose pilot start 2026-04-06, run 2 weeks, results by 2026-04-24, then sizing call week of 2026-04-27. ok?
[38:12] Alex Torres: sounds good.

[39:00] Priya Nair: i'll need traces and realistic prompt distribution. Mina will send. Also we'll need a contact for infra to open endpoints for private testing — jon?
[39:15] Jon Reyes: yes i'll be the infra contact.

[40:30] Sasha Liu: any legal / procurement blockers early?
[40:38] Marcus Lee: standard msas, we can provide EU data residency options, redact PII configs. we'll route contracting through your procurement team.

[41:20] Alex Torres: ok recap please.
[41:25] Marcus Lee: recap: Redwood to send pilot test matrix and Dedicated sizing worksheet by 2026-04-01; Orion send traces and sample prompts by 2026-03-30; pilot planned to start 2026-04-06 for 2 weeks; Redwood to share SOC2/security docs and pricing before pilot. action items noted.

[42:10] Mina Park: quick note — can you include a simulated burst where prefix cache hit is 10%? that's our worst case.
[42:18] Priya Nair: will do.

[43:00] Jordan Kim: thanks everyone.
[43:05] Alex Torres: thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
[43:10] Marcus Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

END TRANSCRIPT
